Added 5 new Content-Length-focused tests to /app/backend/tests/test_submission_preview.py — all 15 tests pass (10 prior preview regression + 5 new). The previous 520 failure mode (StreamingResponse without Content-Length on iframe-loaded PDFs) is fixed end-to-end.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:176 binary_file_response correctly sets Content-Length=str(len(file_bytes)), Accept-Ranges: none, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, and Cache-Control. This buffers the entire file in memory which is fine for the current PDF/DOCX size profile (typically <10 MB) but becomes risky for very large materials in the future — note for capacity planning, not a current bug.

server.py:3317 serve_audio uses an inline Response(...) call instead of going through binary_file_response. Behaves identically and tests pass, but DRY would benefit from passing through binary_file_response(audio_bytes, filename, force_pdf=False) — minor refactor only.

Observed at runtime: Cloudflare overrides backend Cache-Control 'private, max-age=0, must-revalidate' to 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate'. Semantically equivalent (don't cache), so the 520 fix still holds — test was relaxed to accept either form.

FileResponse fallback in serve_audio (legacy disk path, line 3336) does NOT explicitly set Content-Length. Starlette's FileResponse does set it from os.stat though, so this is fine in practice. Worth noting for completeness if disk fallback ever serves prod traffic.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Cloudflare 520 fix verified. The new TestSubmissionDownloadContentLengthHeaders, TestMaterialDownloadContentLength, and TestAudioServeContentLength classes in test_submission_preview.py disable Accept-Encoding (sets to 'identity') so requests doesn't auto-decompress and strip Content-Length — mimicking iframe behavior more closely. If any future change goes back to StreamingResponse(io.BytesIO(...)) without setting Content-Length, these tests will catch it. Note the deprecated fpdf2 'dest=S' warning is harmless and pre-existing.
rca of the issue: Cloudflare 520 reproduced in production from StreamingResponse(io.BytesIO(...)) which omits Content-Length and falls back to chunked Transfer-Encoding. When an iframe loads a PDF, the browser issues a Range request — Cloudflare's proxy receives a chunked response without Content-Length and returns 520 'Web server is returning an unknown error'. Mitigation: introduced binary_file_response() that uses fastapi Response(content=bytes) with explicit Content-Length, Accept-Ranges: none (so browsers don't issue Range requests), X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN (so iframe is allowed), and Cache-Control. Verified end-to-end through the Cloudflare-fronted preview URL: Content-Length now matches body bytes exactly, no chunked Transfer-Encoding.
